chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
regarding a man who died and left his daughter and a sister of his father and mother. He said: 'The wealth is for the daughter, and there is not for the sister of the father and the mother anything.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate when a man leaves only a daughter, a paternal sister, and his mother?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the principle of 'blocking' (hijr) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, where the presence of a daughter excludes the sister and mother from receiving any portion of the estate. It highlights the distinct Shia interpretation of Quranic verses, emphasizing that the daughter takes the entire share as a primary heir in this specific configuration, a ruling supported by the chain of transmission through Zurarah and Ibn Mahbub.
